metadata.note: Modern-day Metra commuter rail network (Chicago), as of the GTFS feed pulled from https://schedules.metrarail.com/gtfs/schedule.zip. Route geometry is real, sourced directly from Metra's own published shapes. Frequency (headway_min) is REAL, computed from actual scheduled trip counts (both directions combined) on a representative Wednesday (2026-08-19) in this feed. avg_speed_kmh is computed from real scheduled trip duration (stop_times.txt) on the representative shape divided by route length. Each route is a single-year segment (2026) since GTFS has no historical depth. Routes with distinct physical branches are split into separate features, matching real Metra branding: Metra Electric District (Main Line / Blue Island Branch / South Chicago Branch) and Union Pacific Northwest (Main Line / McHenry Branch). Rock Island District has two near-duplicate GTFS shape variants sharing the same endpoints; only the higher-fidelity one is used. Historical segments (pre-2026) were added by estimating headway_min at researched ownership/frequency-milestone boundaries (railroad origin dates, RTA/Metra takeover years, electrification, branch cutbacks, etc., sourced from Wikipedia, Metra, and railroad-history sites); unlike the GTFS-sourced 2026 segment and unlike the Amtrak file's historical segments, these older headway numbers are not derived from real historical timetables and should be read as illustrative estimates, not precise data.
metadata.line_label_audit: 2026-08-24: line labels normalised repo-wide to "<operating company>: <line name>" -- the company's common display name (legal suffixes dropped), then the line as a passenger would have known it, or its two terminals where the line carried no advertised name. Long intermediate station lists were reduced to endpoints. For features spanning several operators the company shown is the one that ran the line for most of its drawn years. See CLAUDE.md Rule 6.
metadata.wabash_split_audit: 2026-09-28: metra-sws drew 1893-1993 in Metra colour for trains run by the Wabash (to 16 Oct 1964), the Norfolk and Western (1964-1982) and Norfolk Southern (1982 - 31 May 1993), a Rule 4 defect found by research/branches/wabash_railroad.txt. Those three eras now live in data/wabash_railroad.geojson (wab-/nw-/ns-chicago-orland-park-commuter), drawn Chicago - Orland Park only and from 1913, the first confirmed year (the 1893 start and the "extended to Manhattan by 1909" claim here were unsourced and are not carried over). The 1993-2005 Metra era moved to a new feature metra-sws-orland-park, because the full geometry reaches Manhattan, which the service only reached again in 2006.
